newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz 1996 net profit up around 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Allianz 1996 net profit up around 10 pct.

text.p: (in millions of marks unless otherwise stated)
Group earnings per share 92 vs 87.20 dmk

NOTE - Full name of the German insurer is Allianz AG Holding . Analysts had forecast pre-tax profits in a range of 3.45 to 3.80 billion marks. Net profit forecasts ranged from 2.1 billion to 2.3 billion marks, showing a slower advance than pre-tax because of the lack of the one-off tax break which boosted 1995's net figure.

In a statement, Allianz said the appreciation of foreign currencies accounted for 2.1 billion marks of the increase in premium income while changes in group consolidation caused a 1.3 billion mark drop. Without those changes, premium income would have risen 4.8 percent.
Life and health premium income 30,600 up 1.2 pct
NOTE - Allianz said the slow rise in life and health premiums was due to the exclusion of health unit Deutsche Krankenversicherungs AG, which it sold to Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG in 1996.
Business in Italy and the U.S. showed double-digit growth and Allianz Life of North America saw a renewed rise in demand for single-premium variable annuities.

On non-life business, the company said French, German and Swiss business saw moderate declines while Cornhill in Great Britain and Fireman's Fund in the U.S. raised premiums by between nine and ten percent.
Allianz said the improvement in its underwriting result was due to continued risk selection measures, a favourable claims experience in many markets and a lack of major natural catastrophes.
The non-underwriting result was boosted by positive developments on capital markets, although low interest rates caused a decline in the return on new investments.
